swf_dust_axle.description:
There's a broken axle out on the far straight that's worth more than anything else left on the course.

It's been there two seasons and neither Pim nor the Dustwheel has taken it, and either of them could have, any day, without being seen.
swf_dust_axle.accept_text:
Out past the far turn there's an axle. You'll know it when you see it, because it's the only thing out there that hasn't been stripped.

Go and look at it, and don't bring it back. I'm not asking you to bring it back. Put the scrappers off it while you're there and bring me their tags, because if they've tagged it then it's theirs by their rule. I want to know that for certain rather than suspect it for another two years.
swf_dust_axle.turn_in_text:
They haven't tagged it.

Two seasons and nobody has claimed it, theirs or mine, and now I've got to decide what that means.

It means we both think the other one is going to need it more. That's a stupid thing for two businesses to think about each other, and I've been thinking it since the wet.

Take this to Winnow, who keeps the book. Tell her I sent you and don't tell her why.

swf_dust_cousins.description:
Nobody in Saltwheel calls the Dustwheel bandits. The word has been lying there since the track died and not one person has picked it up.

Grizzik Vane knows exactly why, and she'll say it to you and to nobody else.
swf_dust_cousins.accept_text:
Pim has you putting them off the course and she's right to. I want you to understand what you're doing, though, because she won't tell you.

Half of them are somebody's cousin. When the track died some of us walked into town and some of us walked out onto the pan, and mostly it came down to which way you were facing that week.

Put off the boiler crews and bring me plates off them, and then come back and ask me what we call them. I want to be asked out loud.
swf_dust_cousins.turn_in_text:
There's the same fault in every plate, and it's our fault. They learned it from us, and we learned it from nobody. We worked it out, badly, over eleven years, and then taught it to the people we're now paying somebody to put off a road.

We don't call them anything. That's the answer, and you made me say it.

swf_dust_fuel.description:
Fuel-Trader Mozz laid in enough to run a full season the year before the track died, and he's been sitting on it since.

He's done the arithmetic on who's at fault and he'll do it at you, at length, and the frustrating part is that his numbers are correct.
swf_dust_fuel.accept_text:
Before the sky changed I had two hundred racers on this pan, and now I've got six customers. The same season the mountain turned up in the north, which I'm told is a coincidence, by people who aren't selling fuel.

Go after the wheelmen. They're burning something out there that isn't coming from me, and I want a wheel off one so I can see what it's doing to the rubber.
swf_dust_fuel.turn_in_text:
They're running it dry and lean and getting away with it, which means they've found something cheaper than what I sell.

So that's the rest of my customers gone, in front of me, with a wheel in my hand.

You came through same as the rest of them, and I'm not going to pretend I'm delighted. But you did the job, and this is what the job pays.

swf_dust_ledger.description:
Tally-Clerk Winnow records every cart in and out and every barrel of salt, written down twice. The town is shrinking and she can tell you by exactly how much, which makes her the least popular person in it.

She's been waiting a long time for somebody to ask her a specific question.
swf_dust_ledger.accept_text:
Pim sent you and didn't say why, which means she's finally worked it out and can't stand to be the one who says it.

Bring me their tags and their bars and put them on this bench. Then ask me what column they go in. Ask me the actual question and I'll give you the actual answer, which nobody in this town has wanted since the track died.

The tags I mean are the salvage tags the Dustwheel crews carry.
swf_dust_ledger.turn_in_text:
They go in as customers.

They've been buying fuel off somebody, parts off somebody, and salt off Jixa under a different name since the second winter. It's in this book, and it's been in this book the whole time.

The town is down by a figure I could say out loud. It's not down by as much as it thinks, and the difference is sitting out on that pan calling itself something else.

I'm going to put this in front of Tozzik, and he's going to have to decide whether they can enter.

swf_dust_rights.description:
Salvager Pim Gattle owns everything out on that track the day it stops moving. The rule is written down, it's older than the track, and she's the richest wreck-picker on a pan with no wrecks left on it.

The Dustwheel have been taking things that haven't stopped moving yet.
swf_dust_rights.accept_text:
Read the rule and you'll find it says stopped. That means not slowed, not parked, and not abandoned by a crew that went into town for a season.

Clear them off my course and bring me their bars. Before you tell me that's a lot of effort for a rule nobody enforces, yes, it is. That's what a rule nobody enforces costs, and I've been paying it every season since the wet.
swf_dust_rights.turn_in_text:
Every one of these bars is flattened at the business end, because they've been using them as levers on things that were never meant to come apart.

I'd have taught them that in a morning. Nobody asked me to teach anybody anything.

Grizzik wants a word with you, and she won't enjoy having it.

swf_in_glass_pan.description:
Relic-Keeper Dun can tell you whether a thing came up out of the mesas or down off the mountain. The shard the salt crew brought him did neither.

It's pan fused to glass, and the only pan big enough to do that to itself is four days east of anywhere he's been.
swf_in_glass_pan.accept_text:
Head east, past the last mesa, through the gap and out onto the white.

I'm not asking you to bring me anything, because I've got the shard. I'm asking you to stand where it came from and tell me what's out there. I've been pricing things off that pan for eleven years on the word of carters who never got out of the cart.

The birds will be a problem. Kill all of them, and bring me quills while you're about it. I'll buy those.
swf_in_glass_pan.turn_in_text:
There's a town out there?

Goblins, on a racetrack, on the edge of a salt flat that's eating them, and not one of the carters thought to mention it, because not one of them ever walked past their own cart.

I've spent eleven years treating that pan as weather. Go back out there and find out what they call it.

swf_in_other_end.description:
Namka has a road and somebody to talk to at both ends of it, which she hasn't had in three years.

Caravan-Master Bohl has been looking at the same map and has noticed there's a third end, and that nobody in Freewind Post has ever walked it.
swf_in_other_end.accept_text:
Four caravans a week come up that ramp and not one of them on time, and every one of them comes from the north. Nothing has come from the east in my working life.

There's supposed to be a town out there. Walk to it. Put this in the hand of whoever keeps their books, and let them answer it. Every town has one, and they're always the person nobody talks to.

And kill the Dustwheel scrappers you meet on that road. If I'm sending carts, I want to know what's on it.
swf_in_other_end.turn_in_text:
Winnow reads it twice, which is what she does with everything.

Freewind Post wants to know whether there's anything here worth a cart, and there is. I can tell him to the barrel what there is, and I've been able to for three years. This is the first time in those three years that anybody outside this town has asked me a question.

I'm going to answer it at a length he'll regret. Stay where you are, because you're carrying it back, and you may as well know what this place is while I write.

swf_inn_hinges.description:
Armourer Hett Grindle can slow salt. He can't stop it, and anyone who claims otherwise is selling you grease.

The inn's shutters haven't latched properly in a year, and Vozzi has stopped mentioning it.
swf_inn_hinges.accept_text:
Here's a thing the hives are better at than we are, which I resent and which is true.

Sentinel plate has salt grown right through it and still articulates. Ours seizes in a season. Bring me plates and the wet resin, and let me find out whether it's the plate or what they bed it in.

It's for a shutter. I'm aware of the scale of the ambition.
swf_inn_hinges.turn_in_text:
It's the resin, and the plate is ordinary. They bed every joint in something that never fully sets, so the salt gets in and gets pushed back out every time the joint moves.

That's a hinge that cleans itself by being used. Three years it's been walking past my shop on eight legs.

The shutter at the end latches now. Don't tell her it was me, or she'll want the other eleven done and I've got a trade to run.

swf_inn_no_bird.description:
There's a post outside Saltwheel's inn of exactly the kind a wind rider perches on.

There's never been a wind rider on it. Innkeeper Vozzi Rimehand has explained this to every arrival for eleven years, and she keeps a particular flatness for the purpose.
swf_inn_no_bird.accept_text:
Bed, board and a bind. That's the full list.

Before you ask, there's no wind rider. There was never a wind rider. You came in on your feet and that's how you're leaving.

What I've got is nine birds roosting on the post, because it's the tallest thing in town and they aren't fussy about what it was for. Kill those and bring me quills, and then I'll hear no more about birds from anybody.
swf_inn_no_bird.turn_in_text:
That's them off the post and off my roof.

I've had that post taken down twice and put back up twice, by different people, for different reasons, and neither of them could tell me what the reason was.

It stays up, and I've stopped asking myself why. Your bed is the one at the end, and the shutter doesn't latch.

swf_inn_stock.description:
Quartermaster Dral Wexx laid in eight seasons of stock the year before the track died, for a crowd that was coming and then didn't.

It's all still in the warehouse, in good order, because he's kept it in good order, which is either professionalism or something sadder.
swf_inn_stock.accept_text:
I've got shelves built for a raceday crowd and six regulars. You can do that sum as fast as I can.

The Dustwheel have been into the back of the warehouse twice this season, and I'd rather deal with that than report it. Reporting it means Winnow writes it down, and once Winnow writes it down it's a fact about this town forever.

Put off the boiler crews and bring me their plates and bars. That's what they left behind, and I want it accounted for.
swf_inn_stock.turn_in_text:
That's accounted for, and I'm going to tell you something I haven't told Winnow.

They didn't take anything the second time. They put something back, a crate of plate in our pattern, better made than ours.

So either somebody's out there paying a debt nobody recorded, or they're being polite, and I've got no column for either.

Take what you're owed. The stock was never going to move, and at least it's moving now.

swf_inn_two_years.description:
Vozzi runs the beds and Snod runs the bar, and they haven't exchanged a word in two years.

The business has never been better and both of them have noticed, which is the problem.
swf_inn_two_years.accept_text:
She needs scourers for the pots and she won't ask me for them, and I'm not offering.

So you're going to bring me mandibles and put them behind this bar, where she'll see them when she comes through for the ice. She'll take them, she won't say anything, and that'll be that.

Then ask me what we fell out about. Everyone does eventually.
swf_inn_two_years.turn_in_text:
You want to know what it was.

I don't remember. I've thought about it properly, more than once, in the quiet hours, and it's gone.

I'm certain she remembers. That means one of us is carrying it and it isn't me, and after two years asking her would be the cruellest thing in this building.

She took the mandibles, I watched her take them. Go on, get out of my bar.

swf_item_entry_slip.description:
You turn the slip over. It's an entry for the Saltwheel Open, three seasons out of date, with the name scratched out and written in again twice. It's the same hand each time, pressing harder every go.

Somebody entered, withdrew, entered, withdrew, and entered again, and then the race never happened.
swf_item_entry_slip.accept_text:
The gantry is where entries are taken, and the man under it takes them whether or not anybody brings him one.

Watch for the wheelmen on your way in. They're on the straight at this hour, and they won't step aside for somebody carrying paper.
swf_item_entry_slip.turn_in_text:
Tozzik reads it, and reads it again, and doesn't look up.

That's his hand. He entered the year it died and pulled out, and entered, and pulled out, and entered.

I never processed the third one. It came in after the date and I'm a man who keeps the date, so I put it in a drawer and said nothing, and he's spent three winters believing nobody wanted him on the line.

Nazzik is in the inn. I'm not going over there tonight. I'll go tomorrow, and I'm not saying that to get out of it.

swf_item_sealed_tin.description:
You turn the tin over. It's lead-sealed at every seam, and it was dug up out of pan that's been bone dry for longer than anyone has been counting.

Something rattles inside. Whatever is in it has never once been wet.
swf_item_sealed_tin.turn_in_text:
Nissa holds it up to the lamp and turns it slowly, and she doesn't open it.

That's my seam. It isn't my work, but it's my seam, the double fold. My mother taught me it, her people brought it here from somewhere else entirely, and I've never seen it on anything I didn't make.

It came up out of ground that's been dry for a very long time.

I'm not opening it in front of you, and I'm not opening it tonight. Come back in the spring and I'll tell you what my family was doing under this pan before there was a town on it.

swf_mound_five.description:
Watcher Brak Kesh can see five mounds from the east fence. Three years ago there were two, and the near one was twice as far out.

He says the number in the inn every evening. They've started buying him drinks so that he says it quieter.
swf_mound_five.accept_text:
I count mounds. That's the post, the whole post, and it was invented by a man who expected the number to stay at two.

The skitterers come off the near one and work west along the fence line. Clear a dozen of them off and bring me mandibles, and look at the salt on the mandibles when you take them. It grows over the edge and it doesn't blunt it, and I want to know if that's true of all of them or just the ones I've seen.
swf_mound_five.turn_in_text:
It's true of all of them.

So it can't be damage or age. That's how they're made, and a thing that's made that way on a salt pan didn't end up here by accident.

They belong here now. That's a worse sentence than the number is.

swf_mound_mouths.description:
There are two ways down into the Undercrust and they're most of the pan apart. The Crustfall is a shallow slot by Crustbreak. The Deep Shaft is out under the oldest mound on the map.

Brak has assumed since he took the post that they're two caves.
swf_mound_mouths.accept_text:
I need you at both holes. Go to the Crustfall first, then all the way across to the Deep Shaft, and kill the tunnelers in between them.

I'm not asking you to go in. I'm asking you to stand at both and tell me whether the air coming out of them smells the same. If it does, I've been counting two caves for four winters when there's one, and it's bigger than the pan it's under.
swf_mound_mouths.turn_in_text:
It smells the same at both, so it's one hole.

Most of this pan is standing on one hole with two mouths, and I've been writing two numbers in two columns since the first winter like a man who can't add up.

I'm going to go and say that in the inn tonight at full volume, and they can buy me whatever they like.

swf_mound_moved.description:
The mound Brak calls the near one isn't where it was at the start of the wet.

Mounds don't move. He's checked his own sightings four times and they're good sightings, taken off the same two fence posts since he took the post.
swf_mound_moved.accept_text:
Go out to the First Mound and stand at the foot of it. I need somebody who hasn't been looking at it every evening since the first winter to tell me what shape it is.

Kill the crawlers while you're there and bring me the resin, because the resin is what matters. If they're laying fresh on the west face and the east face is old, then it didn't move. It grew, westward, toward the fence, and that's a different problem with a different arithmetic attached.
swf_mound_moved.turn_in_text:
Fresh on the west and old on the east, so it grew.

It grew toward us, at a rate I can now calculate, and I'm going to calculate it tonight. Then I'll have to decide whether to say the new number in the inn.

They'll buy me drinks either way. That's what I've learned about this town.

swf_mound_queen.description:
One cave, two mouths, and at the heart of it something that's been laying since before anybody in Saltwheel was born.

Brak has stopped counting mounds. He says there's no point counting the branches when you've found the root.
swf_mound_queen.accept_text:
Go in at whichever mouth you like. They both get there, which is the thing I spent three years not knowing.

She's at the middle. Kill the rippers on the way and bring me plates off the sentinels, because I want to see whether what guards her is made the same as what comes out to the fence.

I'm not coming. My one skill is standing on a fence counting, and down there there's nothing to count.

The Undercrust is a long way south of Saltwheel, under the far edge of the pan.
swf_mound_queen.turn_in_text:
They're made exactly the same, root to branch, and she was the root.

It doesn't end it. You know that and I know that. There are four more mounds out there and a hole under all of them.

But the near one has stopped growing west this week, measured off the same two posts. It's the first time the number has gone the other way since I took this post, and I'm going to enjoy it for exactly one evening.

swf_mound_salt.description:
Brewer Nissa Tolk seals everything in lead because salt air takes a cork in a season.

She's been reading Brak's notes over his shoulder in the inn and has noticed something he hasn't, because she's the only person in Saltwheel who thinks about salt as a substance rather than as a price.
swf_mound_salt.accept_text:
Brak counts the mounds, and nobody asks the obvious question, which is what's coming out of them.

The tunnelers bring spoil up and leave it. Bring me loads of it, and more mandibles to set against the spoil.

The pan is salt all the way down, for as deep as anybody has ever dug. If what they're bringing up is dry, we've got a problem nobody in this town is equipped to think about.
swf_mound_salt.turn_in_text:
It's bone dry, all of it, from under a pan that should be wet through at that depth.

So they're digging through what's under the salt, and what's under it has no water in it any more. I'd very much like to know when it stopped having water in it.

Somebody has asked this question before, and it wasn't anybody here. Go and find out where.

swf_mound_spitters.description:
Doc Pellik treats salt sores, sun, and whatever the bugs do to a hand. That's three complaints, in that order, every season.

The third one has been climbing for two years and he's stopped pretending it hasn't.
swf_mound_spitters.accept_text:
A spitter gets resin into a wound and the wound sets. It doesn't close, it sets, with the dirt still in it, and then I'm cutting it open again in a fortnight.

Clear them off the fence line, and bring me sacs still under pressure and scorpid barbs to set against them. The barbs keep their venom wet out here when everything else dries. If I can work out why, I can work out how to keep a wound open.

I know it's crude medicine, but it's the medicine available.

The fence line runs along the Mounds, east of Saltwheel.
swf_mound_spitters.turn_in_text:
They're all still under pressure, which is what I needed.

The barb keeps wet because of something in the sheath, and the resin sets because of something it's missing. Between the two of them I've got an afternoon's work and possibly a hand saved in the spring.

That's the best sentence I've said in this surgery in a year.

swf_open_course.description:
The Mirage Raceway is a loop out across the northern pan and back to the straight. It was surveyed once, eleven years ago, and nobody has walked it since the hives came up.

Tozzik has been posting a course he hasn't seen.
swf_open_course.accept_text:
Go out to the far turn and look at it. That's all I'm asking for, and it's more than I've done.

The darters have taken the north leg, and they come off the ground fast enough to put a driver into the salt. Clear all of them, and bring me resin from whatever is laying it, because I need to know whether the course is fouled or whether something's building on it.

Whichever one it turns out to be decides whether there's a race.

The drones that lay the resin work the Crust, south-west of town, and not the course itself.
swf_open_course.turn_in_text:
Something's building on it. That resin is structural, so they aren't just crossing my course. They're putting something down on it, and the far turn is inside whatever they're putting down.

So the loop is gone, and the straight isn't. A race on the straight alone isn't an Open and I'm going to call it one anyway, and you're the only person who'll ever know that I know.

swf_open_date.description:
Race-Marshal Tozzik Brasswheel posts the times for the Saltwheel Open on the first clear day after the winter wet. Entries at the gantry, scrutineering at noon, flag at two.

Nobody has entered for three seasons. He posts them anyway, in a clean hand, and stands under the board for an hour afterwards in case somebody comes.
swf_open_date.accept_text:
The start line wants clearing before anything else happens, and the ones clearing it aren't mine. They've been off the course stripping the kerb markers since the wet, and every marker they take is a yard of the line I can't certify.

Clear them off the straight and bring me the tags. The tags are numbered, and I want to know which markers I've lost and not just how many.

They're Dustwheel scrappers, and the tags are the salvage tags they hang on whatever they strip.
swf_open_date.turn_in_text:
They're numbered in order, which means one person pulled them in one afternoon and didn't hurry.

I'm not angry about the markers. I'm angry that it took me until the tags to work out nobody had been out to look.

Right, then, scrutineering is at noon and I've got no scrutineer.

swf_open_entries.description:
The board is up, the scrutineer is ready, and the entry column has been blank for three seasons.

Tozzik won't ask anyone directly. He's decided that asking would make it a favour, and a favour doesn't count as an entry.
swf_open_entries.accept_text:
I'm not going round the town asking, but you can. You aren't from here and it costs you nothing, which is the only reason this isn't beneath both of us.

Nazzik holds the course record and will tell you so. Grizzik keeps a crew for a race that doesn't run and pays half of it herself. Mozz has fuel and no one to sell it to.

Ask all three, and don't persuade anybody. I want to know what they say when nobody's leaning on them.
swf_open_entries.turn_in_text:
So that's one record-holder who won't drive, one pit boss who'd crew it tomorrow, and Mozz.

Mozz said he'd supply the fuel at cost on condition somebody tells the newcomers this is their fault. I'm not putting that on a board.

But he said he'd supply it. Write that down and leave the rest.

swf_open_flagfall.description:
Pit-Boss Grizzik Vane has four hands on the payroll for a race that hasn't run since the wet before last. Tozzik pays half and she pays half, and neither of them has ever said out loud what they're paying for.

This week they find out.
swf_open_flagfall.accept_text:
Here's the part nobody says in front of Tozzik. The Dustwheel know the date too. They've been running the straight themselves since the wet, and they'll be on it at two whether we are or not.

So the straight gets cleared properly this time. Put off the wheelmen and the boiler crews, and bring the wheels back. I want the flat-spotted ones, off the machines that were actually driven, because I want to see what they've been doing with my course.
swf_open_flagfall.turn_in_text:
Every one is flat-spotted on one side. They've been locking the wheels at the same mark on every run, which means they're racing each other out there, properly, and timing it.

Three years I've been paying half a crew to sit in a shed, and the sport never stopped. It just stopped being ours.

Go and tell Tozzik the flag drops at two.

swf_open_record.description:
The flag dropped at two. There was one entrant, on the straight alone, because the loop belongs to something else now.

Tozzik timed it himself, because the only other person who knows how was driving.
swf_open_record.accept_text:
Before I post it there's a thing I want done, and I want it done by somebody who wasn't here for the good years.

Walk the straight, end to end, at the pace a person walks. Then go and put the mound-guards off the eastern mark and bring me plates off them, because the eastern mark is where the course used to turn and I want to know what's standing on it now.

I'm going to post the time either way. I'd rather post it knowing.
swf_open_record.turn_in_text:
It's worse than the record by a margin I'm not going to say out loud, on a course a third the size of the one the record was set on.

I've posted it anyway.

Nazzik will tell you his record stands, and he's right. He won't tell you he was under the board at six this morning reading the new time. I saw him, and he saw me see him.

The date held. That's what I had, and I held it.

swf_open_scrutineer.description:
Mechanic Oyla Spannerwick has scrutineered every Open since she was old enough to hold the gauge, and she hasn't been asked since the track died.

She says yes before Tozzik finishes the sentence, which embarrasses them both.
swf_open_scrutineer.accept_text:
If anything runs on that straight it runs on a boiler, and I won't pass a boiler I haven't seen plate from. Bring me pieces off the Dustwheel crews. They're running the same pattern we did and running it badly, which makes their failures useful to me.

Bring me pry bars too. Those aren't for the race, they're for me.

Three years ago somebody drove a machine down that straight with no boiler in it at all, and did the whole run on a thimble of fuel. I've taken one apart since and I understand it now, and that's worse than not understanding it.
swf_open_scrutineer.turn_in_text:
Every one of them is blued in a ring. It's the same fault we had and never fixed, and they haven't fixed it either.

There's a comfort in that I'm not proud of.

Tell Tozzik his scrutineer is ready. Tell him I said it like it was nothing.

swf_salt_back.description:
Caravan-Master Bohl runs four caravans a week up the ramp and not one of them on time.

He's been asked about the Saltwheel road every season since the track died and he's given the same answer every time. This season the answer has changed.
swf_salt_back.accept_text:
Ovi wants a cart on that pan, and I've told her no every season because of what's on the road. I don't mean the hives, I mean the crews.

Clear the Dustwheel scrappers off the west crossing and bring me their salvage tags. If the tags are numbered in sequence then it's one outfit working a route, and I can negotiate with an outfit. If they're scattered then it's nobody, and I can't.

And take Ovi's reply back down with you. She wrote it standing up, which from her is a great deal.
swf_salt_back.turn_in_text:
They're in sequence, so it's one outfit and one route, with a schedule I can read off six tin tags.

I can work with that. I've worked with worse, and I married one of them.

Tell Brinecount the cart comes in the spring, and tell her I said if, in the voice I use for if. She'll know it. Everyone who ships out of a dying town knows that voice.

swf_salt_cart.description:
Road-Agent Fenk Dustle sells what a person needs to walk out of Saltwheel. It's a thriving business, because walking out is the only option available.

He's extremely cheerful about this, and it takes a while to work out why.
swf_salt_cart.accept_text:
Jixa wants her salt in Freewind Post, and there's no cart, no bird and no road worth the word. What there is, is you.

The west crossing goes past the Brine, and the basilisks have the Brine. Kill them and bring me eyes. I sell the eyes to people who think they're lucky, and before you ask, no, they aren't, and they buy them anyway.

Bring me barbs as well. Those actually work for what I say they do, which makes them the odd item on my table.
swf_salt_cart.turn_in_text:
These are clouded right through. Looking into one is like looking down the pan at noon, which is exactly what I tell the buyers and exactly why they buy them.

The crossing is open. Go and tell Jixa, and then come back to me, because she's going to send you across it and you'll want the kit, and I'm going to sell it to you.

There's no bird. I've mentioned that, and I'll mention it again.

swf_salt_crossing.description:
Freewind Post sits over a long drop at the far end of the mesas, and between it and Saltwheel there's a pan, a range, and nothing that flies for hire.

Jixa has been shipping to Spice-Trader Ovi for eleven years, and the two of them have never met.
swf_salt_crossing.accept_text:
These are the sacks, graded and sealed. Ovi has been buying off me since before the sky changed and she's never once haggled, which told me everything I needed to know about her and nothing about what she looks like.

When you get up there, ask her the question I've never been able to put in a letter. She'll know which one. If she doesn't, she isn't the woman I've been trading with.
swf_salt_crossing.turn_in_text:
Ovi turns one of the sacks so the seal faces her, and she doesn't open it.

Eleven years, and she wants to know whether I still think it's boring.

Tell her yes. Tell her I've got three climates on one table now, and the only thing on it that's never caused me a day's trouble is her salt. The mountain can do what it likes as long as the pan keeps drying.

And tell her the caravans will come. Bohl has been saying it for a year, and one of these years he'll be right.

swf_salt_graded.description:
Salt from the shore is clean and salt from the crust isn't, and the difference is money.

Jixa grades it herself, by eye, with a vulture quill, and she's never once been wrong in a way the buyer noticed.
swf_salt_graded.accept_text:
Go out onto the Crust and bring me what the tunnelers have thrown up. It's the deepest salt anybody can get at without digging, and the deepest salt is the cleanest. I've believed that for twenty years on no evidence at all.

And put the scorpids off the drying ground while you're out there. They get into the stacks and they don't come out, and then somebody finds one in a barrel in Freewind Post and I hear about it for a year.
swf_salt_graded.turn_in_text:
That's the cleanest I've graded. Twenty years of guessing and it turns out I was right, which is worth less than being able to prove it, but it's worth something.

Now for the problem.

I've got the best salt I've ever had and no way to get it anywhere, because the cart doesn't come any more.

swf_salt_one_trade.description:
Jixa Brinecount deals in salt. That's the whole business, and everybody laughed at her for twenty years for it.

Nobody's laughing now. Most of them are just gone.
swf_salt_one_trade.accept_text:
Salt is the only trade on this pan the Integration didn't touch, and I'll tell you why, because nobody else here will say a kind word about any of it.

Nothing that came through needed a racetrack. Everything that came through needs to eat.

The vultures are at the drying racks on the shore, and they've worked out that a rack is a table. Kill them, and bring me quills. I use them for marking grades, and I'd buy them off you anyway.
swf_salt_one_trade.turn_in_text:
Every one is salt-stiff, which is what makes them good for grading. They don't bend, so they don't lie about the line they drew.

You'll have heard a lot of complaining in this town and most of that's fair. Mine is the one ledger that went up, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise just to be sociable.

swf_solo_crew.description:
Pit-Boss Grizzik Vane keeps four hands on the payroll for a race that hasn't run since the Integration.

Tozzik pays half and she pays half, and neither has said out loud what they're paying for.
swf_solo_crew.accept_text:
My crew haven't touched a running machine since the track died, and two of them have started forgetting things you can't relearn off a book.

So I'm sending you out to bring me work. Go after the wheelmen and bring me wheels and tags. The wheels go on my benches, my hands strip them and rebuild them and put them on a shelf, and then I pay them.

I'm not doing it for a race. I'm doing it so their hands remember the work.

The tags are the Dustwheel's salvage tags. They tell me which machine a wheel came off.
swf_solo_crew.turn_in_text:
They had all of them apart before I'd finished telling them what they were.

One of them cried about it, in the shed, where he thought I couldn't see. I let him, and then I handed him the second one.

That's my whole management philosophy, and it's never once failed me.

swf_solo_lead.description:
Salt air ruins a cork in a season, so Brewer Nissa Tolk seals everything in lead and charges you for the lead.

She's heard what they say about lead. She'd like you to drink it fast.
swf_solo_lead.accept_text:
Everything I make dies in a cork out here. Clear the crustback scorpids off the drying ground and bring me their barbs. The sheath keeps the venom wet in air that dries everything else, and if I can get at what the sheath is doing, I can stop sealing in lead and stop charging you for it.

I'd like to stop charging you for it. I'd like that on the record.
swf_solo_lead.turn_in_text:
Whatever is in the sheath, it's built into it, not painted on.

That means I can't copy it with what I've got on this bench, and I'll be sealing in lead for another year at least.

Still, knowing I can't do a thing is worth something. It's worth less than doing it, but I'll take it.

swf_solo_prices.description:
Everything on Trader Grebbit Maul's table came across the pan on a cart with four bad wheels.

He'll tell you the price is the wheels, and it's partly the wheels.
swf_solo_prices.accept_text:
You'll think my prices are high, and they are. That's cartage across a dead pan. Before you say it, yes, they were lower four years ago, and yes, that's about when the sky rearranged itself and half my suppliers found more interesting customers.

Get the skitterers out of the stock yard and bring me their mandibles. They're in the sacks, they're always in the sacks.
swf_solo_prices.turn_in_text:
That's them out of the sacks, and I'll drop what I charge you by a bit, and not by as much as you're hoping.

I'm not blaming you personally. I'm blaming the general situation, of which you're a part, and saying that out loud to one person at a time is the only satisfaction available to me.

swf_solo_record.description:
Old Nazzik holds the course record for the Saltwheel Open. It's been eleven years and nobody has touched it.

He'll tell you why before you can work it out, and he gets there first on purpose.
swf_solo_record.accept_text:
The course record is mine. Nobody has touched it in eleven years, and that's because nobody has driven the course in three. I'm aware of that, and it doesn't take the record off me.

Go out to the north turn. There's a marker stone there with a time cut into it, and I want to know whether it's still legible. I'm not going out to look and I'm not going to explain why.

The darters are all over that leg. Clear them while you're up there.
swf_solo_record.turn_in_text:
So you can still read it.

That's good, that's really good. I'll tell you the thing I don't say in the inn. A record only counts while people are trying to take it, and the day they stopped trying it turned into a number on a rock.

Tozzik posted a new time this week, worse than mine by a long way. It's the best morning I've had in a long time.

swf_solo_shrinking.description:
Every cart in, every cart out, every barrel of salt, written down twice.

Tally-Clerk Winnow is the least popular person in Saltwheel, because she's the only one who can answer the question the town asks itself at night.
swf_solo_shrinking.accept_text:
I need spoil and quills. The spoil is to weigh against last year's, and the quills are to write with, because I've used mine up and the general goods has stopped stocking them.

That last part is a data point, and I've recorded it.

Then ask me the question. Everyone wants to and nobody does, and I'd like, once, to be asked rather than avoided.
swf_solo_shrinking.turn_in_text:
We're down by a quarter, over three years, in bodies. In trade it's worse, and I won't say the figure because it isn't mine to hand to a stranger.

People think I keep this book to be unpleasant. I keep it because when a place goes, it goes without anybody writing down what was in it, and I've decided that isn't happening here.

That's all of it. You asked, and nobody asks.

swf_water_answer.description:
The melt is higher every spring on the mountain. Nobody on the mesas can say where that water goes. The pan it should arrive on is drier than its own waterline and dry underneath.

The three of those have never been in one room. You've been in all three.
swf_water_answer.turn_in_text:
These are wet. Every load from the foot of the Deep Mound is damp, out of a pan that's bone dry four miles west of here.

So it arrives, and it's never stopped arriving. It goes under, and it goes east, and it ends up beneath the oldest hive on this pan. That hive has been sitting on the only wet ground in the flats since before the first goblin saw this place, and it's been getting more of it every spring since the range came down.

Nobody made that happen. A mountain arrived, the water it sheds found the lowest thing it could, and the lowest thing was already occupied.

I'm going to write this down and send a copy up the mesas, and in about forty years somebody will read all three parts together and understand this pan.

swf_water_three.description:
The tunnelers bring up dry spoil from under a pan that should be wet through.

Nissa Tolk has been holding that fact for a season, waiting for somebody to bring her a second one, and Oyla has just brought her a waterline.
swf_water_three.accept_text:
So I've got two facts. The pan was deeper, and the ground under the pan is dry. Those don't sit together without a third thing between them, and I don't have it.

Bring me more loads of spoil, from as far east as you're willing to walk, and basilisk eyes. The eyes cloud by taking up whatever's in the air around them. I can read a dry season off one the way you read a ring off a tree, if I've got three to argue with each other.
swf_water_three.turn_in_text:
The eastern spoil is drier than the western, and the eyes agree with each other, and none of this is a Saltwheel-sized question any more.

Water comes off a mountain in the north. It crosses the mesas, and it should arrive here. Somebody on that mountain has been watching their melt get bigger every spring, and somebody on those mesas has been asking where it goes. If you've stood in front of either of them, you already know more than I do.

Come back when you have, and not before. I'd only be guessing, and I'm too old to guess in front of company.

swf_water_waterline.description:
There are shore stacks out on the western pan, lumps of rock the salt hasn't finished eating, and every one of them carries a waterline.

Oyla noticed it with a gauge in her hand, looking for something else entirely.
swf_water_waterline.accept_text:
Go out to the stacks on the west shore. There's a stain round every one of them at a height, and the height is the same on all of them, which means it's a waterline and not a coincidence.

It's a long way above where any water has been in my lifetime. Mark it for me, because the quills take a mark on wet rock and hold it. And put the drones off the stacks while you're at it. They're working the base of them, and I don't want my marks eaten.
swf_water_waterline.turn_in_text:
It's the same height on all of them, to within a hand.

This pan was deeper than this. I don't mean in a story or a song. I mean measurably, at a height I can put a gauge on, and recently enough that the stain hasn't gone.

So where did it go? I'm really asking. I want the answer, and I don't have the range to go and get it.
